speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see this neonate is three days old and presenting with seizures, lethargy, and other neurological signs. To begin our assessment, can you tell me if there were any complications during the birth or if the mother had any fever or infections during pregnancy?

text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of chorioamnionitis, low birth weight, and poor Apgar scores raises a high suspicion for neonatal sepsis or intraventricular hemorrhage. Given the lethargy and tonic seizure, what are your current vital signs, specifically the rectal temperature and blood glucose level? REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, Blood_Glucose, CBC_with_Diff, CRP, and Coagulation_Profile.
